summary: Orbit Intern is a simple, easy-to-follow storytelling game that highlights the necessary steps in conducting a space mission. It incorporates minigames per step and provides concise dialogue aimed to educate everyone at all ages. In a continuously-curious generation but with limited resources pertaining to space education, Orbit Intern helps educate students, professionals, and other people by providing an easy-to-follow yet detailed story of managing and creating a space mission.
details:
Orbit​ Intern is an interactive storytelling game that highlights the different factors and elements in managing and leading a space mission. Through its detailed but concise nature of delivering information, it solves the problem of a lack of space education material that is readily accessible to all. Furthermore, the language level used is designed to be understandable and comprehensive to all, by mostly removing jargon terms (and if they are required, they are explained immediately), so everyone, from children to grandparents, can be able to enjoy space education through Orbit Intern.

​When making this game, we considered accessibility and simplicity as the priority elements for the game, as the main objective of the game was to educate everyone. We also considered repeatability and decision-making, in order for players to actually remember what they learned in Orbit Intern and provide challenging and simple games, leading players to come back and play it again.

In regards to programming and coding, HTML CSS was used for the UI and design, and JavaScript for the game mechanics and art, with some parts being refined by Claude in terms of game mechanics and fixing glitches. As for the design itself, we employed a dark, retro-style motif for our UI, reminiscent of the 80s-90s arcade games that were popular, around the time where space exploration was as its peak.

Now you may ask: what makes our game unique? Well, firstly, our minigames. It isn't tied down to a single theme—it provides modernity and repeatability to the game itself: from the classic game of blasting asteroids to the modern Wordle, the minigames provide something that the players may not expect and provide intellectual stimulation to the learners. Furthermore, its designed simplicity. Other popular games may give you everything but nothing to start with (like sandbox games), leading to frustration and a disinterested feeling, but with Orbit Intern, it may be simple, but it provides you tools and materials embedded into the dialogue and the minigames to make sure that you are learning about space mission and exploration every step of the way.

To sum it up, Orbit Intern is a simple, accessible, entertaining, and educational storytelling game made to educate people of all ages and all cultures about space missions, exploration, development, and discovery, and invoke intellectual stimulation.
